title: Screenplay, every second
judge_notes: screenplay.json is the source of truth (schema: templates/screenplay.json); screenplay.md is the readable copy. Live shots are made by AI image then image-to-video; graphic shots are built in HyperFrames. Every word on screen is an overlay, never inside an AI frame.

questions.text: Does every second from 0 to the end have exactly one row?
Do the shots run from 0 to the end with no gap or overlap, and does every row name the shot playing?
Is every live shot 1-3 s long (graphics at most 4 s)?
Does the voice-over in lines[] say the humanized story's spoken lines word for word?
Do the rows carry the same voice-over words as lines[], second by second?
Is every line timed inside the film, without overlaps, with caption text and spoken text?
Does every caption fit the caption length limit?
Is every live shot's prompt free of requests to draw text, a logo, an emblem or a number plate?
Is every number on screen found in research.md or the brief, or marked Sample?
Does every live shot have a keyframe prompt, a motion, a camera and bibles that exist?
Are the bibles in screenplay.md word for word the same as in screenplay.json?
Does every live shot ask for one small action that fits its length, with nobody entering or leaving frame?
Are hands, phones and products described so they come out right (five fingers, a real grip, phone screens away from the lens)?
questions.evidence: Quote a hand or phone description.

questions.text: Does every sound effect have its picture in the same second, and does the music column describe a voice-free bed?
questions.evidence: Quote one sfx with its screen text.

questions.text: Is every claim on screen or in the voice-over found in research.md's claims list?
questions.evidence: Quote each claim and its research claim.
